title: Prepare for interviews with a simple practice workflow
excerpt: Structure your answer practice, mock interviews, and test preparation so every application has a follow-through plan.
author: CareerBOT Team
body: Most interview prep fails not from lack of effort but from lack of structure. A short, repeatable workflow beats hours of unfocused review.

Start by listing the five questions you're most likely to face for this specific role — usually a mix of "tell me about yourself," a behavioral question tied to the job description, and a technical or scenario question.
For behavioral questions, draft answers using a simple situation-action-result shape. Keep each answer under two minutes when spoken aloud; longer answers tend to lose the interviewer's attention.
Practice out loud, not just in your head. The gap between a mentally-rehearsed answer and a spoken one is usually bigger than people expect — mock interviews close that gap fast.
Finally, debrief after every real interview: write down the questions you were actually asked and how you'd improve the answer next time. That feedback loop compounds faster than generic prep.
